problem_type: The Desktop stdio→HTTP bridge treated a reset on a stale pooled connection as proof that Nomi is not running
symptom: pnpm run gates (full tier) failed on electron/capabilityCore/mcpHostReliability.test.ts 'Nomi 重启（同端口、旧会话号作废）后…' with error -32000 「连不上 Nomi：请先打开 Nomi 再试」 although the restarted server was listening; passed alone, failed 12/12 when 12 copies ran in parallel. (Seen in the pre-push gates lane, which shares the CI test set.)
direct_cause: After a same-port restart the HTTP client's pool still held idle keep-alive connections to the old process. The forwarded tools/list and the bridge's ping probe each went out on one of them and got ECONNRESET (undici 'fetch failed' with cause code ECONNRESET). probeUpstream mapped any status-less failure to 'down', so the first reset ended recovery with NOMI_UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE.
class_root: Two different connection failures were folded into one bucket: 'refused / DNS' (provably never written — Nomi is not there) and 'reset on a reused connection' (ambiguous — Nomi may be there). The repo already has the single verdict for this distinction (electron/outboundDispatchEvidence.ts outboundRequestWasNeverWritten / isTransportLevelFailure), but the bridge classified by 'has an HTTP status or not' instead of using it.

invariant_owner_layer.why: probeUpstream (inside bridgeStdioToHttp) is the only place the bridge decides "Nomi is down" for a status-less failure; it now asks outboundDispatchEvidence and re-probes (ping is idempotent) on transport resets, up to 4 times.

affected_population: Claude Desktop (and any stdio-only host) users whose first MCP call after restarting Nomi was told to open Nomi although it was running
internal_only_reason: The behaviour is our bridge's classification of Node/undici connection errors; undici's cause codes are the evidence, already centralised in outboundDispatchEvidence.ts.
invariants: The bridge reports NOMI_UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE only when a probe failure proves the request was never written (refused / DNS / connect) or after a bounded number of transport resets
A reset on a stale connection never by itself turns into 'open Nomi first'

door_reduction.why_not: classifyUpstreamFailure / probeUpstream are already the single classification door in the bridge (door-map: one write door); the fix routes it through the repo-wide verdict instead of adding a second classifier.

generality_proof: The decision is made from the error's cause chain via the shared verdict, so it holds for every method the host forwards (tools/list, resources/*, tools/call) and every reason a pooled connection goes stale (restart, server-side idle close), not just this test's restart.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single answer to 'was this request provably never written' (also used by paid submission and the MCP loopback RPC).
Single answer to 'is this a connection-layer failure (reset / closed) rather than a reply'.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Already uses outboundRequestWasNeverWritten to decide 'may have run' vs 'not sent'; no change needed.
Treats only ECONNREFUSED as 'no instance' (spawns one); resets are not counted as refused, so it does not have this bug.

recurrence.reason: The bridge was the only classifier that keyed on 'has a status code'; the other connection-error sites already use the shared verdict.
same_class_scan: grep ECONNREFUSED|ECONNRESET|UND_ERR_SOCKET|fetch failed in electron/capabilityCore → mcpNodeLauncher.isConnectionRefused (refused-only), mcpLoopbackRpcCall (shared verdict), mcpHttpBridge (fixed)

legacy_paths.rationale: The old 'any status-less ping failure = down' branch is replaced in place; no parallel path kept.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency change; the SDK's StreamableHTTPClientTransport and undici behave as documented.

migration: None: behaviour change only for status-less probe failures. Hung Nomi (ping timeout) still fails after one probe, as before.
residual_risks: Not exercised against a real Claude Desktop restart; covered by the real-SDK mcpHostReliability test (12/12 parallel runs pass, previously 12/12 failed) and the deterministic unit test.
